I’ve just executed a preview evaluation that programmatically clicked the “Start Session” button in the UI (`showView('interactive'); document.querySelector('#btn-start-session').click();`). The result returned the string “launching”, which indicates that the click event was successfully dispatched and the front‑end should now be attempting to spin up a new container running the native terminal (the TUI) for the Pi provider.

The next logical step is to give the system a moment for the asynchronous backend processes to complete: the UI will send a request to the server, which will start a Docker container, initialize the WebSocket connection, and render the terminal UI inside the preview pane. All of these steps take a few seconds, especially on a fresh container start. If I immediately try to interact with the terminal (e.g., sending keystrokes, querying the DOM, or taking another screenshot), there’s a high chance the container isn’t ready yet, leading to race conditions or errors like “session not found” or a blank preview.

Previously, after starting a session I used a `sleep` pause (e.g., when launching the Pi terminal via the API) to allow the container to boot before proceeding with further checks. I should replicate that pattern here: a short, deterministic wait that ensures the container and its TUI have time to initialize.

The appropriate tool for this is the Bash tool, which can run a simple `sleep` command. I’ll set the duration to 20 seconds—long enough for the container to start but short enough to keep the overall workflow responsive. I’ll also give the command a description (“Wait for container + TUI to start”) so the logs are clear, and set a timeout of 30 seconds to guard against any unexpected hangs.

Thus, the next action is to invoke the Bash tool with `sleep 20`. This will give the UI and backend the needed breathing room before I attempt any further interactions or validation steps.
